title: Bigger flowers with more variety
question: Which bed has the flowers you asked for -- bigger, more varied -- and does the spread read as a stand rather than a random scatter?
context_md:
Round 28, second of two PRs (the first gave petal colour a real locus so it passes parent to seedling). This one: bigger authored heads (herb organ_cluster 9->16, scrambler 5->8, shrub 1->3, shrub's first-ever authored value), a per-individual size multiplier on genome slot 9 (0.3x-1.7x, so a stand shows a real spread rather than one repeated size, heritable like every other shape gene), and herb's petal range widened from two bands to three (yellow/orange/red) so a cross shows a middle colour instead of a coin flip.

**What I already measured, so you don't have to re-derive it**: `labforage scenario=played_bed frames=120000`, three seeds, this build against `main`. The organ economy fires harder across the board -- `organs_built`, `fruit_dropped` and `flowers_rebloomed` are all up, sometimes by a lot. But played-bed plant count at frame 120,000 is down 15-70% against `main` in all three seeds (464/574/303 -> 322/170/259), even after re-deriving the `Ripen` costs so a bigger head doesn't ask more of the shared reproductive budget than it did before. That's reported rather than fixed further -- a gentler size bump wasn't tried for want of time, and standing-flower counts at any one frame ride the rebloom cycle's own phase, so don't read the single-frame numbers below as the whole story; `flowers_rebloomed` (monotonic) is the trustworthy one.

This frame (6,000) is the earliest checkpoint, where the population cost hasn't caught up yet -- it's closest to what a player planting this bed today would first see.
